rv.q: Seeing Jonathan Kent's production for a second time confinns me in the view that this is the best account ofCoward's masterpiece sinceAlan Rickman and Lindsay Duncan struck sparks offeach other in the West End more than a decade ago.
This is a gloriously entertaining evening, opulently designed by Anthony Ward, and offering two hours of comic bliss.
In the second half this becomes high-grade fare.
And although Kent's production was a success at the Chichester festival last year, it appears to have mislaid some sparkle on the journey to London.
The efforts of the director on this occasion can dissipate rather than enhance the comedy, as the actors overdo things in their efforts to get laughs that are there anyway.
Jonathan Kent's scintillating and sexy revival of Noel Coward's sharpest, most piercing portrait of a marriage drains every word of its comic and dramatic potential.
All of this is there in Jonathan Kent's fine production of Private Lives, which has just transferred from Chichester to the West End.

cn.t: Jonathan Kent's dazzling revival of Coward's masterpiece earns praise for its razor-sharp wit and fresh energy. Critics highlight the scintillating chemistry between Toby Stephens and Anna Chancellor in this superb West End transfer from Chichester.
